title: K1 — Marine timekeeper / watch (ZAA0038), Board of Longitude Explorers
locator: One-page object sheet, Description; entire sheet read.
scope_limit: Educational object account establishes commission/completion and named voyage use, not a manufacturing cost series, sea-trial reanalysis or fleet denominator.
evidence_lineage: Curatorial identification of surviving timekeeper ZAA0038 with Board of Longitude project interpretation. Underlying Board records were not independently transcribed in this contribution.

title: Larcum Kendall — obituary, Gentleman's Magazine 60(2), pp. 1213–1214 (1790), transcribed in Cook's Log 40(2), p. 42 (2017)
locator: Complete online transcription, especially paragraphs on copying, 1775 cleaning, third voyage deterioration and simplified successors.
scope_limit: Commemorative, favourable contemporary account; original printed pages and rate records not separately checked. Approximate delivery date about 1771 conflicts with S01's 1769 completion and is not used as an exact chronology.
evidence_lineage: 1790 obituary via a named 2017 society transcription. Its information may derive from Board/Cook reports also underlying S01 and S03; independence is not demonstrated.

title: Longitude
locator: Encyclopedia of the History of Science, April 2021; sections Investing in longitude and Navigation systems, especially notes 20–33.
scope_limit: Research historian's synthesis, not a new voyage-level dataset. Modern backup-navigation claims and general diffusion dates are not used to estimate uptake.
evidence_lineage: Synthesises Newton testimony, Board of Longitude research and scholarship including Dunn/Higgitt, Davidson, Miller, May and navigation histories. Quoted original documents remain mediated unless otherwise specified.

title: Hisashige Tanaka and His Myriad Year Clock
locator: Historical Essays on Japanese Technology, UTCP Collection 6, pp. 31–45; reprint of 2006 article. Inspected pp. 31–41 and appendix heading.
scope_limit: One exceptional clock plus comparative mechanisms. Distinguish observed disassembly from conjectural design history and biographical anecdotes; no sales or clockmakers' employment census.
evidence_lineage: Author participated in study of surviving clock/calendar material; describes 2004 disassembly and measurement with National Science Museum scholars and former Seiko engineers. Career narrative draws on 1931 and 1992 biographies. Those biographies, notebooks and earlier 1949/1969 investigation records were not independently inspected here.

title: What is a Traditional Japanese Clock (Wadokei)?
locator: Entire page, especially opening explanation and Production of mechanical clocks in Japan.
scope_limit: Corporate museum account. Surviving specimens and an institutional chronology do not establish population ownership, uniformity of practice or immediate compliance with the 1873 reform.
evidence_lineage: Museum interpretation based on its clock collection and historical records not individually footnoted. Shares a curatorial environment with materials studied in S04; not independent proof of all historical claims.

title: Archeological Investigation of the Armory Street, Lower Armory Grounds, Harpers Ferry Armory (46JF518)
locator: NPS Regional Archeology Program Occasional Report 21; historical discussion pp. 55–59, notes 221–247; figure 19.
scope_limit: Complete 22 MB report acquired; selected historical sections read. These claims use its documentary synthesis, not the excavations as direct proof of interchangeability. Hall's rifle works and the musket factory must be distinguished.
evidence_lineage: Historical passages depend on Merritt Roe Smith, Charles Snell, Peter Schmidt and Stuart Brown; p. 56 test account is mediated through Schmidt, p. 59 gauge history through Smith. Report also contains original archaeology, which is not treated as independent corroboration of those documentary claims.

title: John H Hall
authors: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park, National Park Service
locator: Entire page, updated 23 September 2019; 1819 contract, Hall letter of 20 December 1822, Talcott statement of 1832.
scope_limit: Short institutional account with celebratory framing. Hall's claim of economy and ordinary-worker production is testimony, not an audited cost or worker-income estimate.
evidence_lineage: Quotes Hall and Talcott via a bibliography including Smith, Hounshell and Huntington; archival originals not checked. Shares the Smith evidence family with S06.

title: African Motors: Technology, Gender, and the History of Development
locator: Open-access full PDF acquired from the page's Download PDF link; selected Chapter 2, Overhaul: pp. 94–99, 118–121, 136–142 and table 2.1, pp. 138–140.
scope_limit: Entire book available, only stated sections inspected. Historical interviews are retrospective; one month of apprenticeship plus return visits is not a representative workshop census or controlled repair durability test. Male-centred archive does not establish all women's participation.
evidence_lineage: Original oral histories with named mechanics (mostly 2011–2012 in the cited sections), photographs, archives and author apprenticeship. Table 2.1 names interviews for each repair. Author's earlier Modernization Bubu work shares this research programme, so references to it in S09 are not independent replication.

title: Resilience from Below: Technicians, Repair and Maintenance Works in Post-socialist Dar es Salaam, 1985–2020
locator: HoST 16(1), pp. 73–98; inspected method p. 78, pp. 81–88 and 91–97; DOI 10.2478/host-2022-0005.
scope_limit: Original qualitative study, no representative denominator, appliance failure-survival sample or engineering validation of voltage-protection claims. The article's electricity-grid and appliance tasks are distinct; this case centres appliance use, with labour-transition claims explicitly marked as an interpretation.
evidence_lineage: Author's anonymised Kiswahili interviews from 2018 and 2020, newspaper letters, Tanesco reports and historical scholarship. Garage-history discussion inherits Grace/Brownell; some utility labour/network claims inherit Degani/Ghanadan. Only the direct appliance testimonies are treated as this study's independent field observations.

title: The TEA Set: Tacit Knowledge and Scientific Networks
locator: Science Studies 4(2), pp. 165–185; inspected empirical sections pp. 171–183, especially pp. 172–173, 176–177, 180–183; DOI 10.1177/030631277400400203.
scope_limit: Contemporary qualitative investigation of a deliberately selected emerging technique. Snowball search supplemented by three searches for isolates; not randomised contact or investment. Paper explicitly admits that successful written-only reconstruction is possible.
evidence_lineage: Original interviews and laboratory visits starting with seven British laboratories in summer 1971, followed by North American source laboratories; researcher sometimes participated in communication. Full PDF is an institutional teaching copy of the journal scan. S11 is a follow-up by the same sociologist with a laser-building participant, not independent replication.

title: Building a TEA Laser: The Caprices of Communication
locator: Social Studies of Science 5(4), pp. 441–450; publisher-displayed footnotes 2, 8, 10 and 11 inspected. Main narrative not available.
scope_limit: Only displayed footnotes support claims: simultaneous variable changes, teaching burden and power-unit failures. Do not infer the full build sequence or outcome from inaccessible body text.
evidence_lineage: Coauthored follow-up involving the builder's own experience. Same Collins research programme as S10; partially different episode, not independent confirmation of an all-purpose tacit-knowledge theory.

title: Box of U.S. Rifle Model 1841 Inspection Gauges (View 4), HAFE 7427
authors: National Park Service, Museum Management Program
locator: Complete museum object record, date ca. 1846, attribution to Major William A. Thornton, catalog HAFE 7427.
scope_limit: Museum attribution and physical object are evidence of inspection equipment, not independently measured tolerances or evidence of all factory output meeting them. Thumbnail was not used for metrology.
evidence_lineage: NPS custodial catalogue for the same surviving gauge set illustrated in S06 figure 19. This is object-level corroboration with explicit shared material, not a second independent gauge-adoption history.
